kitDescription: Scarlet is a Pilgrim Burst III assault-rifle Attacker who buys damage with her own health. Every 10 landed normal shots she gains a self ATK buff of 23.15% that stacks up to 5 times for 5 seconds, and each of those activations shaves 4.01% of her current HP, so she steadily wounds herself as she fires. The wounds are the point: once her HP drops under 60% she permanently gains 6.61% Critical Damage, and once it is under 50% her burst grants her 19.57% Critical Rate for 10 seconds on top of its main effect. That burst hits all enemies for 849.15% of her final ATK. She also has a 30% chance to strike back for 138.24% of final ATK whenever she is attacked, so a fight where she takes hits both accelerates her thresholds and adds a small retaliation damage channel.

redAssertions: scarlet S1 / 'the 5 sec window really expires between procs' — asserts stretching durationSec 5→60 must raise the total; total is identical, so it fails. Classified RECON_ERROR: at the datamined cadence (12/s, ammo 20, reload 159f ⇒ ~4.63 rounds/s ⇒ a proc every ~2.16s of firing, max inter-proc gap ~3.5s across the reload) the 5s window never lapses and the stack pool sits 5/5 permanently under the SSOT refresh-on-reapply rule (game-mechanics §11). The S1 atkPct block is byte-identical in the driver, the S6 blind override and the parser baseline, so the assertion fails against every faithful encoding of this unit — it is a blind-test over-specification keyed to a slower cadence, not a driver divergence. All 19 other S5 assertions pass; the 2 skips are the two correctly-unmodeled GAP lines.

gotchas.summary: The burst's 'Activates when HP falls below 50%' gate is not represented at all — the 19.57% crit-rate buff fires on EVERY cast, including casts made at full HP. Documented ⚑, not a silent drop.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: '■ Affects self. Activates when HP falls below 50%. Critical Rate ▲ 19.57% for 10 sec.' The driver's own derivation puts the 50% crossing at ~37s (17 procs × ×0.9599 current-HP decay); controlComp gives scarlet ~6 casts in 180s, so the first cast (~12s) is credited a 19.57pp crit-rate window it should not have. Major-bucket impact: +19.57pp × critBonus ≈ +0.11 inside a Major of roughly 2.5–2.6 for 10s of one FB window ⇒ order 0.5–1% of her 180s total. Driver: ungated + flagged (caveat 4). S6 blind: IDENTICAL choice, same flag. S2b blind (fable): FIX — gate it on a proc-count resource pool.
gotchas.suggestedFix: The engine primitive exists and the driver already prototyped it (resource pool + resourceGate, proven on soda-twinkling-bunny). Unlike the S2 ramp, this gate has a discrete, footage-observable signature — does crit rate appear on burst #1? — that a proxy cannot express, so the literal encoding is strictly more expressive at the same evidence cost (both rest on the identical unmeasured ⚑ crossing). Land the resourceGate at the ⚑-derived proc-17 threshold, keep the ⚑ on the threshold itself, and pin the crossing from a focus video (HP bar + first orange-crit popup after her first two casts). Do NOT retune the drain or the threshold to move the board.

gotchas.summary: The HP<60% step-on for the 6.61% Crit Damage buff is modeled as a 56s linear ramp; the equal-integral argument holds in TIME but not in damage-weighted terms. Documented ⚑.
gotchas.evidence: Kit: '■ Activates when HP falls below 60%. Affects self. Critical Damage ▲ 6.61% continuously.' A 0→full linear ramp over 2T integrates to a step at T over [0,2T] (arithmetically correct: T≈28s ⇒ rampSec 56), but damage is concentrated in Full Burst windows (×1.5 major) rather than uniform in time, so the substitution is only approximate in delivered damage. Driver: rampSec 56 + ⚑2. S6 blind: IDENTICAL rampSec 56, same flag. S2b: FIX via resourceGate.
gotchas.suggestedFix: Same resource-pool gate as above (a real step at the ⚑ crossing removes the shape approximation entirely). Magnitude of the buff itself is kit-true at 6.61 and needs no measurement; only the crossing time does — same recipe (HP bar + first crit-damage-tier popup from a focus video).

verdictRationale: GO. All 6 kit lines are FAITHFUL (3) or DOCUMENTED_GAP (3) — 6/6 = 1.00 — with every skip verbatim in `unmodeled`, no `ignored` effects, all three slots declared, and every ⚑ carrying an estimate, a tier and a measurement recipe. Convergence is mechanically RED on exactly one S5 assertion, and that assertion is a RECON_ERROR, not a divergence: 'the 5 sec window really expires between procs' requires stretching durationSec 5→60 to raise the total, but at the datamined cadence (~4.63 rounds/s ⇒ max inter-proc gap ~3.5s) the stack pool sits 5/5 permanently under the SSOT refresh-on-reapply rule, so the assertion fails identically against the S6 blind override and the parser baseline — it cannot distinguish a faithful encoding from any other. The three independent derivations (S2b fable spec, S5 blind test, S6 blind override) agree on every magnitude, stat key, scope, duration and trigger; the only substantive disagreement is HOW to represent the two HP thresholds, and the driver's adoption of the opus-convergent rampSec/ungated proxy over fable's literal resourceGate is a documented modeling choice resting on the SAME unmeasured ~28s/~37s crossing, not a faithfulness defect. Ranked for the owner: (1) the ungated burst crit-rate gate (med — ~0.5–1% of her total, and unlike the S2 ramp it has a discrete footage-observable signature the proxy cannot express, so the already-prototyped resourceGate is the better landing); (2) the S2 ramp's time-vs-damage-weighted integral (low). Both are documented ⚑s and neither blocks GO. Two of the driver's three stated reasons for the proxy are sound; the third — 'the GO criterion needs the S5 blind test green' — is not, since choosing an encoding to satisfy a grader is fit-to-the-grader and the avoided failure was itself a cadence artifact; the choice survives on reasons (1) and (2) alone. Same-model residual the owner should spot-check: every agent here is the same model family and all three converged on treating unobservable-HP gates as always-on/ramped, so the strongest sanity check is footage — when does her crit visibly turn on, and does burst #1 crit at the boosted rate? Two further unverified premises ride under it: the ⚑1 cadence tuple (a 20-ammo AR at 27.08% per shot is a non-standard fire-mode tell, and the permanent 5/5 = +115.75% ATK steady state depends entirely on it — a materially slower true cadence would let stacks lapse), and the 'Current HP ▼' compounding-vs-flat-of-max reading, which moves both derived crossings ~6s earlier if flat.
